To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we report a diverse spectrum of 1q21 deletions and duplicatons and provide detailed clinical information for each patient.
diverse, recurrent deletations and duplications at 16q21.1 are associated with distinct clinical manifestations, and the recurrent duplications at proximal 16q21 are likely pathogenic.
recurrent deletions and reciprocal 1q21 duplications have been associated with distinct disorders, including chromosome 1q deletion syndrome, chromosome dup(1q) syndrome, and TAR syndrome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the clinical characterization of patients with diverse, recurrent deletional and duplicational variants at 1q.21.1.
diverse and recurrent 1q21 duplications and deletions, and provides a comprehensive characterization of the disorders associated with 1q21 variants.

the characterization of the clinical phenotypes and genomic breakpoints associated with diverse, recurrent deletional and duplicational variants at the 1p21.1 region, which may help in the understanding of the pathophysiological mechanisms and the genetic etiology of the disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
deletions at the 1.5-Mb proximal region of 1q21, duplications at a 1.1-Mb region of 1.5 Mb, and duplications at a ~0.7-Mb region of the proximal 2.2 Mb are causative in patients.
deletions and duplicating at the 1p21.1 region are associated with diverse, recurrent disorders.

recurrent deletions at the distal 1q21 region are associated with chromosome 1q deletion syndrome and TAR syndrome, and recurrent duplications at 3' of the distal 2q21.1 segmental duplication are associated with chromosome dup(1q21.2q23).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
deletions at the distal 1q21, duplications at proximal 1.21, and deletions/duplications at the distal proximal 1.q21 regions are associated with distinct disorders.

the recurrent deletions and/or duplications at 3.5 Mb of the subchromosomal region at 1q22.1 are associated with distinct disorders, which are chromosome 1q22 deletion syndrome, chromosome1q21.2 duplication syndrome, TAR syndrome, and a novel disorder associated with the proximal 3.5-Mb duplications at 22.1 region.
recurrent, variable deletions and duplicational variants at 1q.21.1 locus are likely to be causative for a variety of disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
recurrent, pathogenic deletions and duplica-tions at the 1 q21.1 region can be associated with diverse clinical features and thus may be misdiagnosed as other disorders.

the clinical manifestations associated with 1q21 deletions, duplications, and duplications at 9q34.3 are not mutually exclusive, and the disorders are likely caused by haploinsufficiencies of the genes at the respective regions.
the 1q deletion syndrome and TAR syndrome are not distinct disorders, and the clinical spectrum of these disorders is much more extensive than what has been reported in the literature.
